subject: math

entries: Completing the square, as area - x^2 + 6x is an x-by-x square plus two 3-by-x strips, and the missing 3-by-3 corner of area 9 completes the square.
slots.label: Completing the square
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The discriminant decides the roots - D = b^2 - 4ac: positive means two crossings, zero means one touch, negative means the curve misses the real axis.
slots.label: The discriminant
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Quadratic inequalities on a number line - find the roots -2 and 2 for x^2 - 4 > 0, then test each region to get x < -2 or x > 2.
slots.label: Quadratic inequalities
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: a negative discriminant means no solution - no real roots is not no solution, because the two roots are complex.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: For ax^2 + bx + c, the quantity D = b^2 - 4ac; its sign decides the roots: positive gives two real roots, zero gives one repeated root, negative gives no real roots.
slots.label: Discriminant
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Rewriting a quadratic as a perfect square plus a constant by adding the missing corner: for x^2 + 6x, half of 6 is 3 and the missing corner is 3^2 = 9.
slots.label: Completing the square
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A value of x that makes the quadratic equal to zero; on the graph it is where the parabola crosses or touches the x-axis, and a negative discriminant still leaves two complex roots.
slots.label: Root
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An inequality such as x^2 - 4 > 0, solved by finding the roots that split the number line into regions and testing a value in each region.
slots.label: Quadratic inequality
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A root involving i, where i^2 = -1; a quadratic with a negative discriminant has two complex roots, such as x = i and x = -i for x^2 + 1 = 0.
slots.label: Complex root
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: A-Math quadratics: completing the square, discriminant and inequalities
